dependencyGate.transitiveGate: T16 depends on accepted T14 and T15 and transitively on T06 contracts/DTO and migration/test foundations.
dependencyGate.beforeGate: Only this synthetic fixture plan is prepared. Do not implement attachment/storage behavior, connect PostgreSQL or S3, run behavior tests/builds/migrations, or claim provider/database acceptance before dependencies are accepted.

harnessBoundary.syntheticInputs: Use only symbolic workspaces WA/WB, devices D1/D2, upload IDs U1/U2, attachments A1/A2, and opaque ciphertext-byte canaries. No plaintext, real account, signed URL, credential, bucket, or user object is included.
plannedHarnesses: After T16 acceptance, use isolated PostgreSQL with non-owner NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS roles, transaction barriers, ledger snapshots, and recording HTTP/session/device adapters.

Use an object-storage fake for application state-machine faults only. A fake cannot satisfy staging/final conditional-write, signed-header, immutable-version, CopyObject embedded-error, or deletion-confirmation provider gates.
Run provider-specific conditional PUT/COPY/version-delete acceptance only against a disposable isolated AWS S3 bucket with synthetic ciphertext and expiring credentials; no production or user bucket.
forbidden: Production/shared PostgreSQL, real workspaces, accounts, user files, credentials, or buckets.
Mock-only evidence reported as S3 conditional-write/version/delete behavior acceptance.
Client-visible PUT permission for final object keys, multipart expansion, content-hash dedupe across workspaces, or plaintext server processing.
Releasing reserved/staging/pending-final bytes or object counts before physical deletion is confirmed.
Changing quota limits, lock order, immutable source version, final-key write permission, or usage-event idempotency to make a fixture pass.

cases.setup: Seed synthetic WA/D1 and WB/D2 with separate ledgers and entitlements.
cases.action: D1 reserves through WA path, then attempts WB path, mismatched path/body wid, and a WB attachment identifier.
assert: Only WA can receive an upload lease; cross-workspace attempts are non-disclosing 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.
Mismatched route/body scope produces no upload, signed URL, ledger delta, or usage event.

cases.setup: Prepare synthetic reserve DTOs at exact cipher-byte and purpose-specific limits from the frozen spec.
cases.action: Try unknown fields, malformed UUID/decimal/base64url, invalid nonce/hash lengths, unsupported purpose, and one-byte-over payload.
assert: Frozen invalid DTO/envelope/decimal errors are returned; no storage URL or ledger write occurs.
Cipher size is bounded by the applicable plaintext limit plus the fixed 16-byte tag; image_thumb also obeys maxImageBytes.

cases.setup: Provide server-derived workspace entitlement and a request containing forged client plan/cloudBytes fields.
cases.action: Submit the reserve request with forged entitlement fields and then with the adapter's trusted entitlement.
assert: Unknown fields are rejected or ignored only as the frozen DTO explicitly specifies; client values never increase the trusted quota.
A rejected request creates no reservation, URL, or usage event.

cases.setup: Start from a ledger with room for one upload and a stable reserveOpId/body.
cases.action: Submit the same reserveOpId and exact body concurrently and sequentially.
assert: Both callers observe the same upload identity and no duplicate signed lease with a new upload identity.
Reserved bytes/object slots and usage events increase once only.

cases.setup: Persist a reserveOpId with one immutable request body.
cases.action: Reuse that reserveOpId with a changed attachment, purpose, nonce, size, key identity, or checksum.
assert: Return 409 IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH without changing the original upload, URL, ledger, or usage event.

cases.setup: Give WA enough remaining quota for either synthetic request alone, but not for both together.
cases.action: Synchronize two distinct concurrent reservations at the workspace/ledger lock boundary.
assert: Exactly one reserve succeeds and one returns 507 QUOTA_EXCEEDED.
Logical/reserved/staging/pending-final and object counts remain non-negative and reconcile with the single committed upload.

cases.setup: Set synthetic live/staging/pending/reserved object counts one slot below or at maxStoredObjectsPerWorkspace.
cases.action: Reserve one attachment and repeat the same reserve request.
assert: A new reserve accounts for both staging and final-candidate object slots before a URL is issued.
At insufficient capacity return the frozen 507 object-limit result; retries add no slots.

cases.setup: Fill WA to maxPendingUploadsPerWorkspace with unexpired synthetic reservations.
cases.action: Attempt one additional reserve, then expire a reservation without confirming object deletion and retry.
assert: A 507 response blocks the extra reservation without over-allocation; exact code/limitKey for maxPendingUploadsPerWorkspace remains OPEN_QUESTION.
Reservation expiry does not clear still-possible physical staging/candidate occupancy.

cases.setup: Start from a valid synthetic reserve request and provider capability record.
cases.action: Inspect the returned UploadLeaseV1 and the signed staging PUT requirements.
assert: The URL targets staging only and expires according to uploadUrlSeconds; reservation expiry uses uploadReservationSeconds.
Signed required headers include the immutable-create condition and frozen size/checksum semantics that the chosen provider actually enforces.

cases.setup: Create one synthetic staging lease in an isolated disposable provider bucket.
cases.action: PUT the same synthetic ciphertext N times with the signed If-None-Match:* condition, then retry with the condition removed or changed.
assert: Only one physical staging object version can be created; repeats fail conditionally or signature validation.
A client cannot remove/change the signed condition or bypass the bucket policy; fake-provider results do not pass this gate.

cases.setup: Persist a reservation, then expose the matching synthetic staging object to the observation worker.
cases.action: Run the worker once and replay its observation event.
assert: Observed bytes move from reserved to staging accounting without dropping the reservation before terminal ready/failure.
Duplicate observation does not add bytes/object count or duplicate the usage event.

cases.setup: Reserve frozen expected size/hash and stage synthetic objects with wrong size, wrong ciphertext checksum, or over-limit bytes.
cases.action: Attempt finalize for each object, then fail or retry physical cleanup.
assert: No invalid object becomes ready or referenced.
Actual staging occupancy remains counted until provider deletion is confirmed; the fixture does not invent an unspecified transport error code.

cases.setup: Create a valid unexpired reservation while its single bounded staging PUT has not completed or produced a verified immutable object version.
cases.action: Call finalize before the upload completes, then observe ledger state while the signed write window remains live.
assert: An incomplete/unobserved upload never creates a ready attachment or final object.
Reservation and possible physical staging occupancy stay accounted until the upload is terminal and any required object deletion is confirmed; no unspecified exact error code is asserted.

cases.setup: Create a reservation with an unobserved or still-present staging object and advance beyond reservation expiry and signed URL expiry independently.
cases.action: Attempt finalize and run cleanup before and after signed_until, including a delete failure.
assert: Expiry closes finalize/new signing but does not release physical staging/candidate accounting by itself.
No final release occurs before signed_until and confirmed version deletion; a still-valid old URL cannot recreate an object removed too early.

cases.setup: Create the staged synthetic ciphertext and record its immutable VersionId or equivalent verified immutable completion identity.
cases.action: Finalize while attempting source replacement/deletion around HEAD and copy.
assert: Finalize copies the exact frozen immutable staging version and validates actual size/checksum.
HEAD followed by copy of a mutable key alone is insufficient; final key is never disclosed as a client PUT target.

cases.setup: Block the first synthetic finalizer after it commits the copying candidate and releases DB locks.
cases.action: Start a second finalizer for the same upload while the first is copying.
assert: The second caller receives 409 UPLOAD_IN_PROGRESS and no second candidate is allocated.
After the first succeeds there is one ready attachment and one usage event.

cases.setup: Pause synthetic HEAD/COPY calls and observe workspace, ledger, and upload locks from another transaction.
cases.action: Hold the provider call while another bounded DB operation attempts the same workspace.
assert: No PostgreSQL transaction/row lock is held across object-storage network I/O.
The persisted copying candidate and pending-final reservation remain visible and accounted during the pause.

cases.setup: Use the selected SDK against a disposable bucket with one immutable synthetic source version.
cases.action: Exercise destination If-None-Match:* on CopyObject, replay against an existing candidate, and inject/observe a 200 response carrying an embedded S3 error.
assert: The actual selected SDK enforces destination conditional creation and copy retry reuses the same candidate.
The full response body and follow-up HEAD/checksum/version are validated; HTTP 200 alone never creates ready state.

cases.setup: Pause after successful candidate copy but before final ready transaction; preserve its key/version and pending-final ledger entries.
cases.action: Crash the worker, then replay compensation/finalize while the exact candidate already exists.
assert: The candidate remains billable and discoverable; retry HEADs and verifies the same candidate rather than creating another copy.
Exactly one ready attachment and usage transition are committed after verification.

cases.setup: Provide matching immutable staging/final synthetic objects and a verified copying upload candidate.
cases.action: Commit ready state, replay finalize, and separately delay staging cleanup.
assert: Ready attachment bytes/hash/version match the verified final object; reserved/pending-final move to logical/live once.
Staging remains charged until its exact version deletion is confirmed; repeated finalize returns the same attachment with zero delta.

cases.setup: Seed ready, deleting, deleted, and foreign-workspace synthetic attachments.
cases.action: Request each download lease as WA/D1 and WB/D2.
assert: Only same-workspace ready attachments yield a short-lived GET URL and frozen ciphertext byte/hash metadata.
Foreign-workspace lookup is non-disclosing; deleting/deleted/not-ready objects do not receive a usable URL.

cases.setup: Create a ready attachment without a version_attachments reference after a synthetic crash boundary.
cases.action: Query usage and run only the frozen GC eligibility calculation.
assert: An unreferenced ready attachment remains charged and cannot accumulate as free storage.
GC does not remove an object while any current/history/trash/snapshot/change-log reference exists.

cases.setup: Race creating a new version attachment reference against a collector that is preparing a zero-reference ready object.
cases.action: Pause both transactions at workspace→ledger→attachment lock acquisition and resume in both orders.
assert: Only the transaction that observes the serialized ready/reference state can commit; deleting objects reject new refs as ATTACHMENT_NOT_READY.
An attachment is never resurrected and byte/object deltas follow the committed physical state.

cases.setup: Seed an object with multiple synthetic provider versions and a delete marker.
cases.action: Delete without VersionId, delete selected versions, inject delete failures, and confirm with provider HEAD/list semantics.
assert: A delete marker or partial delete never releases ledger bytes/object counts.
Release occurs only after all required physical versions are confirmed absent; use of exact VersionId is verified with the real provider.

cases.setup: Commit cleanup_pending with one outbox event and its unique usage-event key.
cases.action: Deliver cleanup repeatedly, crash after physical delete but before DB acknowledgement, then replay.
assert: Repeated compensation is idempotent and cannot double-decrement usage or duplicate a business event.
Failed cleanup remains retryable and charged until deletion confirmation.

cases.setup: Place one unregistered synthetic object and one same-hash object in WA/WB storage inventories.
cases.action: Run reconciliation without a user-facing download request.
assert: Unregistered objects enter a restricted quarantine/cleanup workflow and are not returned to clients or immediately treated as free.
No global ciphertext-hash lookup or cross-workspace deduplication occurs.

cases.setup: Use one synthetic attachment shared by current/history/saved versions, a trash head, and a valid snapshot/change-log pin; make the head 100 days old at deletion time and include a historical version past versionHistoryDays.
cases.action: Delete the old head, advance time across history and trash retention, clear a collection relation, and run GC while each independent reference is present and then removed.
assert: The attachment remains billable while any current, retained-history, trash, snapshot, or change-log reference remains.
A 100-day-old head moved to trash is retained until deleted_at + trashDays even if older than versionHistoryDays.
Clearing a collection relation never deletes its saved target; physical bytes release only after all references and retention gates end and provider deletion is confirmed.

openQuestions.question: The task card cites S09-S15 while current 03 §10 maps upload, quota, copy, and GC behavior to S13-S18; confirm the exact card-to-spec acceptance mapping before T18 acceptance.

The chosen object-store provider and SDK must prove non-removable conditional staging PUT, immutable source-version copy, destination If-None-Match:*, embedded-error parsing, and exact version deletion. No provider capability is assumed by this plan.

03 §9 freezes the 507 quota/storage/object-limit error family; the exact code and details.limitKey for maxPendingUploadsPerWorkspace overflow are not specified. Assert 507 and no allocation until the field mapping is frozen.
